glossary.Knesset: Israel's parliament. It has 120 seats, so a government needs at least 61 to pass laws and survive.
glossary.coalition: A government formed by several parties that agree to work together because none won a majority alone.
glossary.impeachment: A formal process where a legislature charges a sitting leader with wrongdoing and can remove them from office.
glossary.house arrest: Being confined to your home by the authorities instead of being held in prison.
glossary.trilateral talks: Negotiations with three parties at the table, rather than just the two sides of a conflict.
glossary.Yellow Vests: A French protest movement, gilets jaunes, that began in 2018 over fuel taxes. It's named after the hi-vis vests every French driver must carry.
glossary.ANC: The African National Congress, Nelson Mandela's party. It has led South Africa since the first democratic elections in 1994.
glossary.apartheid: South Africa's system of legal racial segregation, from 1948 until the early 1990s.
glossary.MMP: Mixed-member proportional voting. Each party's share of seats closely matches its share of votes, so single-party majorities are rare.
glossary.Strait of Hormuz: The narrow channel between Iran and Oman. Roughly a fifth of the world's oil passes through it.
glossary.magnitude: How much energy an earthquake releases. The scale is logarithmic, so a 6 releases about 32 times more energy than a 5.
glossary.aftershocks: Smaller quakes that follow a big one, sometimes for days or weeks. A strong one can damage buildings already weakened.
glossary.Canary Islands: Spanish islands in the Atlantic, about 100 km off the coast of Morocco and Western Sahara.
glossary.midterms: US elections held halfway through a president's term, for all House seats and about a third of the Senate.
glossary.chief of staff: The president's most senior aide, who runs the White House and controls who gets the president's time.
glossary.press secretary: The White House spokesperson, who briefs reporters on the president's behalf, usually daily.
glossary.Uyghurs: A mostly Muslim, Turkic-speaking people from Xinjiang in western China, where rights groups document mass detention.
glossary.Revolutionary Guards: Iran's most powerful military force, separate from the regular army and answering to the supreme leader. It also runs intelligence and cyber units.
glossary.Sanaa: Yemen's capital. The Houthi movement has controlled it since 2014.
glossary.Houthis: An armed movement from northern Yemen, backed by Iran, that controls the capital and much of the north.

editions.line: Ukraine talks resume in Abu Dhabi, France blames Iran for a fridge hack, and South Africa's ANC hits a new low.

stories.short: Ukraine, Russia and the US talk again
stories.hed: Ukraine, Russia and the US hold their first joint talks since February
stories.body: Negotiators from Ukraine, Russia and the US met in Abu Dhabi for the first {three-way talks|trilateral talks} since February. They talked for nearly 4 hours, and the US called the first day "very productive". A ceasefire is not on the table, according to the New York Times, and the main sticking point hasn't moved: Ukraine wants security guarantees, which Russia rejects.
stories.why: It's the first time all three sides have sat down together in nine months, in what is Europe's biggest war since the Second World War. Expectations are low, but any progress would matter to millions of people.
stories.ctx: Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022. Three rounds of US-led talks earlier this year produced no breakthrough.

fig.u: of talks on the first day, according to NPR. Three earlier rounds this year brought no breakthrough.

stories.short: France blames Iran for a fridge hack
stories.hed: France says Iran hacked supermarket fridges and spoiled tons of food
stories.body: France says hackers from Iran's {Revolutionary Guards} took over the refrigeration controls at around 700 shops in October, turning up temperatures at night and spoiling tons of chilled and frozen food. Paris summoned Iran's ambassador and will seek European sanctions. Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot said France ruled out "nothing" in its response. Iran denies it was behind the attack.
stories.why: It's a rare case of a government publicly blaming another for attacking something as ordinary as the food supply. It shows how everyday connected equipment, like a shop's freezers, can become a target.
stories.ctx: Western governments have accused Iranian-linked hackers of attacks before, usually on government or industrial systems. Proving who is behind a cyberattack is hard, which is why public blame like this is unusual.

fig.u: shops, roughly, whose fridges and freezers France says were taken over in October.

stories.short: A new parliament, but no government
stories.hed: Israel's new parliament is sworn in with no government in sight
stories.body: Israel's new {Knesset} was sworn in on Tuesday. Opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot has the first chance to build a {coalition} and replace Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. Reports differ on whether his side already has a majority, but the opposition hopes to use parliament quickly, including to set up a commission into security failures.
stories.why: If Eisenkot succeeds, it would end the long era of Netanyahu, Israel's longest-serving prime minister. Who chairs parliament could decide how fast that happens.
stories.ctx: No Israeli party ever wins a majority alone, so governments are coalitions of several parties. Eisenkot is a former head of the military.

fig.u: of the 120 seats are needed to form a government.

stories.short: Nvidia's boss and an alleged spy
stories.hed: Nvidia's boss admits an affair with a woman accused of spying for China
stories.body: Jensen Huang, head of the chipmaker Nvidia, admitted to an affair with a business executive who, according to the New York Times, US intelligence believes was gathering information for Beijing. Nvidia is investigating whether he was targeted, and President Trump says the FBI is looking into it. China dismissed the claims as a smear.
stories.why: Nvidia makes the chips behind the AI boom and is worth more than $4 trillion, so questions about its security reach well beyond one company.
stories.ctx: The US limits sales of its most advanced AI chips to China. The Times says the affair has put a spotlight on a murky trade in smuggling those chips into the country.

fig.u: Nvidia's market value, which makes it one of the biggest drivers of the stock market.

people: Founder and chief executive of Nvidia

stories.short: A bid to impeach Pete Hegseth
stories.hed: A Republican moves to impeach the US defence secretary over Iran
stories.body: Thomas Massie, a Republican congressman from Kentucky, introduced eight articles of {impeachment} against Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth on Monday. He accuses Hegseth of waging the war in Iran without approval from Congress and of abusing his powers. Hegseth called it a "political spectacle" and a farce that will fail. Massie is retiring after losing a primary to a challenger backed by President Trump.
stories.why: It comes days after Republicans lost both chambers of Congress in the {midterms}, and tests how far the party is now willing to break with the administration over Iran.
stories.ctx: In the US, the House votes to impeach, which is like bringing charges, and the Senate then holds a trial. The Congress elected last week doesn't take its seats until January.

fig.u: articles of impeachment, or formal charges, that Massie filed against Hegseth.

stories.short: Steel plant blast kills at least 17
stories.hed: An explosion at a Turkish steel plant kills at least 17 workers
stories.body: An explosion and fire tore through the Habaş iron and steel plant in Aliağa, in western Turkey's Izmir province, on Monday. Witnesses said the blast felt like an earthquake. Turkey's president put the death toll at 16, while the BBC and Euronews report 17. The victims were factory workers, and rescuers have been clearing a collapsed platform.
stories.why: Turkey has long struggled with workplace safety, and the blast will bring fresh questions about how heavy industry is inspected.
stories.ctx: Aliağa, north of the city of Izmir, is one of Turkey's main heavy-industry hubs, home to steelworks, an oil refinery and a ship-breaking yard.

fig.u: people killed, according to the BBC and Euronews. The president's count was 16.

stories.short: The ANC's worst result ever
stories.hed: South Africa's ANC suffers its worst election result ever
stories.body: The {African National Congress|ANC} won 30.76 percent of the vote in last week's local elections, its weakest result since the end of {apartheid}, the electoral commission said on Sunday. No party won outright in many towns and cities, so rival parties will now have to share power. Corruption, joblessness and infighting have all cost the party support.
stories.why: The ANC led the fight against white minority rule and has dominated South Africa ever since. Falling below a third of the vote shows how much trust it has lost.
stories.ctx: In 2024 the ANC lost its national majority for the first time and had to form a coalition government with its rivals.

fig.u: of the vote went to the ANC, its lowest share ever.

stories.short: The "cruise for life" runs aground
stories.hed: A "cruise for life" ends with the ship seized in Singapore
stories.body: The Odyssey was meant to sail guests around the world for years. Instead its operator, Villa Vie, ran out of money, the ship dropped its passengers in Cambodia, and Singapore's port authorities have now seized it under a court order won by its creditors.
stories.why: A reminder that "forever" is a big promise, especially at sea.
stories.ctx: Residential cruises sell cabins a bit like flats, with people living on board for years while the ship circles the globe.

quiz.q: What does France say Iranian hackers took over?
quiz.x: Supermarket fridges. France says around 700 shops had their refrigeration controls turned up at night, spoiling tons of food.

quiz.q: Where did Ukraine, Russia and the US meet for talks?
quiz.x: Abu Dhabi. It was the first three-way meeting since February, in the United Arab Emirates.

quiz.q: Roughly what share of the vote did South Africa's ANC win?
quiz.x: About a third. It took 30.76 percent in local elections, its worst result ever.

glossary.Revolutionary Guards: Iran's most powerful military force, separate from the regular army and answering to the supreme leader. It also runs intelligence and cyber units.

editions.line: A deadly shooting in Kraków, the worst day in Yemen for months, new US strikes on Iran, and a pope back on the road.

stories.short: Six killed in the historic main square
stories.hed: A gunman kills six in Kraków's historic main square
stories.body: A gunman opened fire in Kraków's Main Market Square on Saturday, killing six people and wounding about 15. Police shot him and took him to hospital, then found three more bodies at his home. Poland's interior minister says he held far-right, ultra-nationalist views, and Prime Minister Donald Tusk called it an act of terrorism.
stories.why: It's Poland's deadliest shooting in decades, in a country that has long seen itself as safer than much of western Europe. A British national is among the dead.
stories.ctx: Kraków is Poland's second-largest city and one of its most visited. Its main square, Rynek Główny, is one of the largest medieval town squares in Europe.

fig.u: people killed and about 15 wounded. Three more were found at the attacker's home.

stories.short: One of the deadliest days of the war
stories.hed: Airstrikes kill dozens in one of Yemen's deadliest days in months
stories.body: Houthi officials say at least 33 people, mostly women and children, were killed when airstrikes hit homes in a village near the capital, {Sanaa}. They blame Saudi Arabia, which has not commented. A separate attack on a market in Taiz province reportedly killed about 30 more, and each side blames the other for it.
stories.why: Fighting between the {Houthis} and Yemen's Saudi-backed government reignited in August after a long lull. Civilians are paying the price, and observers fear a UN-backed truce is collapsing.
stories.ctx: Yemen's war began in 2014, when the Houthis seized Sanaa. A Saudi-led coalition intervened in 2015 to back the government, and the conflict became one of the world's worst humanitarian crises.

fig.u: people killed across Yemen in 24 hours, according to the New York Times.

stories.short: More US strikes, and a squeeze on land routes
stories.hed: The US strikes Iran again and moves to cut its land supply routes
stories.body: President Trump says the US carried out a new round of what he called "minor" strikes on Friday, targeting an Iranian air defence system. Iranian media reported explosions on Qeshm Island in the {Strait of Hormuz}. Washington has also set up a task force to stop Iran moving weapons over land, and is offering a $20m reward for information on its nuclear programme.
stories.why: Trump says talks with Tehran are making progress, yet the strikes keep coming. The US is trying to squeeze Iran while negotiating, a risky mix that could tip into a wider war.
stories.ctx: The US and Iran are in open conflict, much of it around the Gulf. Iran's nuclear programme has been at the centre of tensions with the West for more than two decades.

fig.u: US reward for information about Iran's nuclear programme.

stories.short: Trump reshapes his team after losing Congress
stories.hed: Trump reshapes his team after losing Congress
stories.body: Days after Democrats won control of Congress in the {midterms}, President Donald Trump named Stephen Miller as his new {chief of staff}. He has also asked Dana White, head of the Ultimate Fighting Championship, to be White House {press secretary}. White says he will meet Trump on Monday to talk about it.
stories.why: With Democrats running both chambers, Trump faces investigations and blocked bills. Promoting a loyal fighter like Miller suggests he is preparing for battle rather than compromise.
stories.ctx: Midterms fall halfway through a president's four-year term. Every seat in the House and about a third of the Senate are up for election, and the president's party often loses ground.

fig.u: chambers of Congress now controlled by Democrats.

people: Named White House chief of staff

stories.short: Floods sweep through tent camps
stories.hed: Heavy rain floods the tents of tens of thousands in Gaza
stories.body: Torrential rain flooded the camps where displaced families in Gaza are living, soaking tents, mattresses and belongings overnight. Local authorities say tens of thousands of people are now without shelter, and fuel shortages are slowing the response.
stories.why: Winter is only starting. Most of Gaza's population lives in makeshift shelters that offer little protection from rain or cold.
stories.ctx: Most of Gaza's roughly two million people have been displaced since the war between Israel and Hamas began in October 2023, and much of the territory's housing has been destroyed.

fig.u: tents flooded within hours, according to local authorities quoted by the Times of India.

stories.short: The Pope travels weeks after cancer surgery
stories.hed: Pope Leo starts a Latin America tour three weeks after cancer surgery
stories.body: Pope Leo XIV began a 12-day tour of Uruguay, Argentina and Peru, three weeks after surgery for lung cancer. He said he was in "fairly good shape". About 40,000 people welcomed him in Paysandú, Uruguay, where he said peace is possible.
stories.why: It's a test of the Pope's health and a homecoming of sorts. Leo, the first American pope, spent two decades as a missionary in Peru.
stories.ctx: Uruguay is often called the most secular country in Latin America, which makes it an unusual first stop for a papal visit.

fig.u: three countries: Uruguay, Argentina and Peru.

stories.short: A 5.7 quake injures more than 20
stories.hed: A magnitude 5.7 earthquake shakes central Japan
stories.body: A {magnitude} 5.7 earthquake struck Shizuoka prefecture at 1:04am on Sunday, injuring more than 20 people. No tsunami warning was issued, but authorities warned that strong {aftershocks} are possible over the coming days.
stories.why: Japan builds for earthquakes better than almost anywhere, so a quake this size rarely does major damage. The warning about aftershocks is the part to watch.
stories.ctx: Japan sits where four tectonic plates meet and gets about a fifth of the world's strongest earthquakes.

fig.u: on the magnitude scale. Each whole step up releases about 32 times more energy.

stories.short: Snow falls in late spring
stories.hed: Spring snow dusts south-east Australia
stories.body: A cold blast brought unseasonable snow to parts of New South Wales, Victoria and Tasmania. The ski resorts at Thredbo, Perisher and Mount Hotham all saw falls, and so did kunanyi/Mount Wellington above Hobart.
stories.why: November is late spring in Australia, so snow is a surprise even in the mountains.
stories.ctx: Seasons are flipped in the southern hemisphere: Australia's summer officially starts on 1 December.

quiz.q: What did Poland's prime minister call the Kraków shooting?
quiz.x: An act of terrorism. Donald Tusk used the word after six people were killed in the main square.

quiz.q: Which three countries is Pope Leo visiting?
quiz.x: Uruguay, Argentina and Peru. It's a 12-day trip, three weeks after his cancer surgery.

quiz.q: Who did Trump ask to be White House press secretary?
quiz.x: Dana White, head of the UFC. Stephen Miller is the new chief of staff.

glossary.Sanaa: Yemen's capital. The Houthi movement has controlled it since 2014.
glossary.Houthis: An armed movement from northern Yemen, backed by Iran, that controls the capital and much of the north.

editions.line: Israel's opposition gets its chance, a bank collapse topples a president, and France marches.

stories.short: Netanyahu's rival gets the first shot at power
stories.hed: Netanyahu's rival gets the first shot at forming a government
stories.body: Last week's election left neither Benjamin Netanyahu's bloc nor his opponents with a majority. On Saturday, President Isaac Herzog handed the job of forming a government to opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot instead of Netanyahu. Eisenkot now has 28 days to put together 61 seats in the 120-seat {Knesset}.
stories.why: If Eisenkot pulls it off, Netanyahu's long run in power ends. He will likely need the backing of Arab-led parties, which would be a big shift in Israeli politics.
stories.ctx: No party ever wins a Knesset majority alone, so every Israeli government is a {coalition}. After an election, the president picks the person most likely to reach 61 seats. Netanyahu is the longest-serving prime minister in Israel's history.

fig.u: of 120 seats needed to govern. Eisenkot has 28 days.

stories.short: A bank collapse brings down the president
stories.hed: A bank collapse brings down Paraguay's president
stories.body: Ueno Bank, which had ties to the state, collapsed and froze the savings of millions of people. President Santiago Peña resigned, was {impeached|impeachment} by Congress and put under {house arrest}. On Saturday he appeared before prosecutors and was charged over the scandal.
stories.why: Peña's government had allowed the bank to expand quickly before it failed, so the anger is aimed squarely at the people in charge.
stories.ctx: Paraguay is a landlocked country of about 7 million people between Brazil, Argentina and Bolivia. Peña, a conservative, took office in 2023.

fig.u: of the country was left unable to get into their bank accounts.

stories.short: Strikes on the power grid before peace talks
stories.hed: Russia hits Ukraine's power grid days before peace talks
stories.body: Russian strikes damaged a major bridge and energy sites around Kyiv, wounded nine people and left parts of the city without power or water. President Volodymyr Zelenskyy accused Moscow of trying to push Ukraine into a blackout. Delegations are due at {three-way talks|trilateral talks} in Abu Dhabi next week.
stories.why: Knocking out power as winter arrives puts pressure on ordinary people. Doing it right before talks is a way of showing strength at the table.
stories.ctx: Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022. Attacks on the power grid have come back every winter since, bringing rolling blackouts.

fig.u: people wounded. Talks in Abu Dhabi are due next week.

stories.short: 140,000 march over the cost of living
stories.hed: More than 140,000 march across France over the cost of living
stories.body: Anti-government protests spread across France on Saturday. Police fired tear gas in Paris and Lyon, and {Yellow Vest|Yellow Vests} protesters defied a ban on their rally, leading to arrests. The government has promised an extra €4 billion for education.
stories.why: France is paying more and more interest on its public debt, which leaves the government little room to spend its way out of the anger.
stories.ctx: France has a long tradition of mass street protest, from 1968 to the pension reform marches of 2023.

fig.u: people marched across France on Saturday.

stories.short: The ANC heads for its worst result ever
stories.hed: South Africa's ANC heads for its worst result ever
stories.body: With about 80% of ballots counted in local elections, the {African National Congress|ANC} is on track for its lowest vote share in history, almost 14 points below 2021. Voters are angry about water outages, power cuts and poor local services.
stories.why: These results show how far the party that ended {apartheid} has fallen, and how much everyday services now decide votes.
stories.ctx: The ANC won every national election from 1994 until 2024, when it lost its majority for the first time and formed a coalition government.

fig.u: points: the ANC's drop since 2021, with 80% of ballots counted.

stories.short: An election too close to call
stories.hed: New Zealand's election is too close to call
stories.body: Early results from Saturday's general election point to a deeply divided parliament. The National party looks set to be the largest, but nobody has a clear path to a majority. {Coalition|coalition} talks could take weeks.
stories.why: With no clear winner, smaller parties get to decide who governs, and they'll ask for their own priorities in return.
stories.ctx: New Zealand uses a voting system called {MMP}, which almost always produces coalition governments.

fig.u: of coalition talks likely before a government forms.

stories.short: Two giant pandas make their debut
stories.hed: Two giant pandas from China make their public debut
stories.body: Ping Ping and Fu Shuang met the public at Zoo Atlanta this week. They are the first giant pandas at the zoo after a two-year gap.
stories.why: Pandas are loaned by China, and sending them abroad has long been a sign of goodwill between countries, sometimes called panda diplomacy.
stories.ctx: Almost every giant panda in a zoo outside China is on loan, and cubs born abroad are usually sent back to China.

quiz.q: Who now has 28 days to form Israel's next government?
quiz.x: Gadi Eisenkot. Herzog is the president who handed him the job, ahead of Netanyahu.
A bank collapse. Ueno Bank's failure froze the savings of millions of people.

quiz.q: Where are Ukraine and Russia due to hold talks next week?
quiz.x: Abu Dhabi. Russia's strikes on the grid came just days before them.
